findings.title: Imported feed HTML is stored and served without sanitization
findings.body: `import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `Post#cook` returns that raw HTML unchanged. Feed items are passed directly to this method by `PollFeed`, so a `<script>`, event handler, iframe, or other active markup in an RSS/Atom item is persisted and rendered with `raw post.cooked` in the embed and normal topic views. A compromised feed or untrusted content included by a feed can therefore execute JavaScript under the Discourse origin, including in an administrator's session. Sanitize imported HTML with the normal allowlist/cooking pipeline (or a strict dedicated sanitizer) before storing it, rather than bypassing cooking.

findings.title: Direct article retrieval does not load open-uri before calling open
findings.body: `import_remote` calls `open(url)` but this file does not require `open-uri`. The only new `require 'open-uri'` is in `Jobs::PollFeed`, which is not loaded on the normal embed retrieval path when feed polling is disabled. In a normal process where nothing else happened to load it, Kernel#open treats the HTTP URL as a file path and raises `Errno::ENOENT`, so requested embeds can never be imported. Require `open-uri` in this dependency's own file (or use an explicit HTTP client).

findings.title: Remote retrieval follows redirects without validating the final destination
findings.body: The host check in `TopicRetriever` only validates the original embed URL, but `open(url)` follows HTTP redirects. An allowed embed host with an open redirect (or a compromised allowed host) can redirect the worker to localhost, cloud metadata addresses, or other internal services; their response is then imported into a public topic. Validate every redirect target against an allowlist and block private/reserved IP ranges, or disable redirects and fetch only the validated origin.

findings.title: Controller success spec expects a synchronous retriever that the controller never invokes
findings.body: This example sets an expectation on `TopicRetriever.new` and `retrieve`, but `EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` instead of constructing a `TopicRetriever`. The expectation is therefore unsatisfied and the added controller spec fails whenever it runs. Update the test to assert the `Jobs.enqueue` call (and cover execution in the retrieve-job spec), or change the implementation if synchronous retrieval was intended.
